item.title: Engie to buy UK Power Networks in $14 billion deal
item.description: French utility acquiring one of United Kingdom’s largest electricity distribution networks. Deal subject to regulatory approval with completion expected mid-2026. Engie says transaction in line with company’s broader electricity network infrastructure ambitions.

item.title: Ireland adds 1 GW of solar in 2025
item.description: Ireland reached 2,345 MW of installed solar capacity by December 2025, more than tripling installed capacity since 2023, according to Solar Ireland data. The country's development pipeline has currently reached 1.7 GW.

item.title: Latvia deploys 258 MW of PV in 2025
item.description: With Latvia’s cumulative solar capacity reaching 920 MW by end of 2025, the Latvian Renewable Energy Alliance says the 1 GW threshold may now have been surpassed. The country also appears on track for a record year in solar deployment this year, as some of the largest projects in the pipeline materialize.

item.title: South Korean railway operator signs solar deal with Qcells
item.description: Korea National Railway has signed a memorandum of understanding with South Korea’s Qcells to expand solar deployment across railway assets as part of its energy transition strategy.

item.title: India installs 7.1 GW of rooftop solar in 2025, residential demand surges
item.description: Residential consumers drove 76% of India’s rooftop solar growth last year under the PM Surya Ghar program, pushing total capacity to 20.8 GW.

item.title: The future of solar is unwritten
item.description: Whatever decision the U.S. Department of Commerce makes on polysilicon imports, some market segments are in for a bumpy ride in 2026 as the expiration of tax credits and other policy levers change the trading environment faced by residential installers and others. Jesse Pichel and Lev Seleznov of Roth Capital assess what lies ahead for U.S. solar.

item.title: US national lab highlights inverter approach as cheaper alternative to DTT
item.description: “Direct transfer trip,” a costly approach to ensure that distributed generation shuts down during a power outage, can make solar projects uneconomical. A US national lab report points to a combination of inverter-based approaches as a viable alternative.

item.title: Australian startup scaling up printed solar technology
item.description: Kardinia Energy has secured AUD 2.15 million from the Australian government’s Industry Growth Program to scale up its flexible, low-cost printed solar technology from university proof-of-concept to pilot manufacturing.

item.title: New model reveals pathway for land-efficient U.S. solar expansion
item.description: McGill University researchers used deep-learning computer vision to analyze 719 solar projects across the Western U.S. The study establishes a new “land-sparing” benchmark, providing developers with precise data to balance rapid capacity expansion with conservation and land-use priorities.

item.title: Ideal Heating launches new monobloc propane heat pump for commercial buildings
item.description: The UK-based manufacturer has expanded its Ecomod 290HT range with a new 65 kW monobloc air-source heat pump using R290 refrigerant, offering flow temperatures up to 70 C, a COP of 4.6, and cascade capability of up to 7 units.
